newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-ARGENTINA NEARER WORLD CUP FINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINA NEARER WORLD CUP FINALS.

text.p: Argentina, who have suffered several hiccups in the World Cup qualifiers, took a big step toward next year's finals in France when they beat Peru 2-0 on Sunday and their other rivals all drew.
Argentina were benefited when the games between Uruguay and Colombia, Venezuela and Bolivia and Ecuador and Chile all ended in 1-1 draws.
The results enabled them to move into the second place in the nine-team South American group and increase the gap between them and the chasing pack.
Colombia, who are third, will also have been happy with their result in Montevideo after losing their previous three games and complicating what had once seemed the easy task of qualifying.
Chile, who play five of their remaining six games at home, overcame the high altitude of the Ecuadorean capital Quito and the absence of star striker Ivan Zamorano to gain a prize point.
Paraguay, who did not play, lead the group with 23 points from 10 games, with Argentina on 19 and Colombia on 18.
All three now appear well placed to qualify, with the fourth place likely to go to any one of Bolivia, Ecuador, Uruguay, Chile or Peru, who are separated by only one point.
Chile may be favourites because of their remaining fixtures while Bolivia have only one home game left.
Goals either side of halftime by Hernan Crespo and Diego Simeone gave Argentina a win after Peru had initally looked capable of forcing a draw.
Argentina were often uninspired in a rough game, in which lenient Brazilian referee Claudio Cerdeira overlooked numerous rough challenges.

Argentina playmaker Ariel Ortega limped off injured in the second half after receiving a battering from the Peruvian defence. Argentina, however, were no angels and a tougher referee would have sent off at least two of their players.
Argentina have recovered after losing in Bolivia and Ecuador and dropping points at home to Paraguay and Chile.
Coach Daniel Passarella has chopped and changed the team and bewildered fans by leaving striker Gabriel Batistuta out of the squad. He was again missing on Sunday.

Ecuador, who under Colombian coach Francisco Maturana are aiming to reach their first World Cup, took a first half lead through striker Ariel Graziani in a game played at 2,800 metres above sea level.

Chile were without Zamorano, who picked up a second yellow card in addition to the five goals he scored in April's 6-0 thrashing of Venezuela. However, they still managed to hit back through Marcelo Salas in the second half.

Uruguay, who won the World Cup twice in its early days, got the perfect start when Dario Silva shot them in front in the seventh minute but failed to capitalise, despite a good first-half performance.
They paid the penalty when Hamilton Ricard, standing in for the suspended Faustino Asprilla, equalised early in the second half.

Venezuela picked up only their second point in 11 games against Bolivia. Ramiro Castillo scored for Bolivia, who had gone behind to a Giovanni Savarese goal, but was sent off near the end for punching an opponent.
